questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

I’m sure I ______ them at the party last night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'**saw'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**last night**" in the given sentence **indicates** that the sentence is in the simple past tense, therefore the past tense form of the verb should be used.
 
• Let us explore the given options__:
 __
 
• 'Am seeing' is the present continuous form of the verb.
 
• 'Was seeing' is the past continuous form of the verb.
 
• 'Saw' is the simple past form of the verb.
 
• 'Have seen' is the present perfect form of the verb.

 
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

**Complete Sentence__:** *I’m sure I **saw** them at the party last night*.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

The bus ______ before I reached the bus stand.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is had left.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If two actions take place in the past in succession, the structure is given below:

 
 
• ​1st action- Past perfect tense i.e. Sub + had + V3 + Obj.
 
• 2nd action- Simple past tense i.e. Sub+ V2 + Obj.
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *The patient had passed away before the surgeon arrived.*
 
 
 
• Thus in the blank part of the given question, 'had left' will be used as it is the 1st action in the given sentence.

 

Correct Sentence__: *The bus **had left **before I reached the bus stand.*

• The past perfect is a verb tense used to talk about actions that were completed before some point in the past.
 
• The formula for the past perfect tense is had + [past participle].

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The captain dropped the trophy while he ________the victory with his teammates.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires **the past continuous tense to indicate an action that was ongoing at the time another action occurred.**
 
• The **past continuous tense** is formed using **"was/were" + the present participle (verb + -ing).**
 
• In this case, **"was celebrating" **correctly indicates that the celebration was in progress when the trophy was dropped.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The captain dropped the trophy while he **was celebrating** the victory with his teammates."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "celebrated"** – This is the simple past tense, which does not convey the ongoing nature of the action.
 
• **Option 3: "is celebrating"** – This is the present continuous tense, which is not appropriate for past events.
 
• **Option 4: "celebrates"** – This is the simple present tense, which is not appropriate for past events.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• In this context**, "promote"** is the most suitable choice because it means to support or actively encourage a cause or venture.
 
• **The sentence** suggests that by joining the networks, one can help to improve or enhance (i.e., "promote") better Governance.
 
• The term** "Governance"** usually refers to the processes of interaction and decision-making among the actors involved in a collective problem.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'Join our networks to promote better Governance.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's the explanation for each option:
 
 
• **"Drain"** - This verb generally means to cause the water or other liquid in something to run out, leaving it empty, dry, or drier. In a metaphorical sense, it can mean to exhaust or deplete resources, which is not a positive or appropriate action for improving Governance.
 
• **"Disintegrate"** - This verb means to break up into small parts or to cause something to do this, usually as a result of impact or decay. It implies destruction or the breaking down of something, which does not align with the goal of bettering Governance.
 
• **"Sedate" **- This verb means to administer a sedative to someone or to calm them down. In a metaphorical sense, it could imply pacifying or suppressing activity. It doesn't make sense in this context because it doesn't suggest any action that would improve Governance.

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with an appropriate option.**

How can seawater from the oceans be ______ fresh water that is suitable for people to drink?
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Turned into**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"turned into" **is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
 
• It indicates **the process of transforming or converting seawater from the oceans into fresh water that is suitable for drinking.** This phrase signifies a change in the state or composition of the water to make it usable for consumption.
 
 
• *​"How can seawater from the oceans be **turned into**__ fresh water that is suitable for people to drink?"*
 
 
 
• This sentence raises the question of how the conversion of seawater to drinkable freshwater can be achieved. It implies a transformation or treatment process that removes the salt and impurities from seawater, making it safe for human consumption.
 
• In summary, the most appropriate option is **4) turned into**, as it accurately conveys the transformation of seawater from the oceans into freshwater suitable for drinking. The other options do not align with the intended meaning and context of the sentence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Now, let's examine the other options:
 
• **change about:** This option does not convey the intended meaning of converting seawater into freshwater. "Change about" implies altering or modifying something in general, but it does not specifically address the transformation of seawater into drinkable freshwater.
 
• **surrender in:** This option does not accurately represent the process of converting seawater into freshwater. "Surrender in" conveys the act of giving up or yielding, which is unrelated to the topic of water treatment.
 
• **minced on: **This option is not relevant to the context of converting seawater into freshwater. "Minced on" means to cut or chop into small pieces, which does not pertain to the process of purifying seawater for drinking.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

The children had made a mess on the floor, so I asked Sana to clean _________ up.
questions.solution:
'It' is used to refer to a place, animal or thing.

For example:

*It is blue in colour.*

'They' is used to refer to two or more people or things. 

For example:

*They were in the room a minute ago.*

'Them' is used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to two or more people.

For Example:

*They have taken their families with them.*

'Its' is used when something is belonging or relating to the same thing.

For example:

*Their house has its own swimming pool.*

In the given sentence, 'it' will be referred to as the mess that has to be cleaned.

Correct Sentence:

The children had made a mess on the floor, so I asked Sana to clean **it** up.

Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the correct indefinite article to fill in the blank.

My neighbour is ______ passionate photographer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **a**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this question, the blank requires an **indefinite article**.
 
• The word **"passionate" **starts with a **consonant sound**. However, the word "photographer" does not affect the choice of the article.
 
• Indefinite articles "a" and "an" are used before singular nouns. The choice depends on whether the following word starts with a vowel sound or consonant sound.
 
• The word "passionate" starts with a **consonant** sound, so the correct indefinite article is **"a."**

Correct sentence: *My neighbour is **a passionate photographer**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indefinite Articles:**

 
 
• **"a":** Used before words starting with consonant sounds (e.g., "a cat," "a dog").
 
• **"an":** Used before words starting with vowel sounds (e.g., "an apple," "an hour").
 
 
 
• **Definite Article:**
 
 
• **"the":** Used to refer to specific nouns (e.g., "the car," "the book").

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to ﬁll in the blank.

This is the girl ______ is going to IIT, Delhi.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

Whom is used instead of ‘who’ as the object of a verb or preposition.

For eg; Whom is she talking to?

That is used to identify a specific person or thing observed or heard by the speaker.
